evidence.text: [Colour] Hale & Whitford LLP brand palette: navy #1B2A41 (primary), burgundy #6B1E2E (accent), cream #F4EFE6 (background), brass #B08D57 (details). Teal is strictly prohibited, as confirmed by Priya Raman on 2025-02-10. Additionally, Margaret Hale specified on 2025-04-11 that burgundy must be used only as an accent color and never as a background color; Priya Raman reaffirmed this on 2025-08-04, noting that burgundy backgrounds appear too alarming and warning-like, and mandated that only navy or cream backgrounds are permitted. As of 2025-06-06, Margaret Hale has approved the use of a cream background and a thin navy rule for website hero banners. On 2025-06-16, David Whitford rejected the use of thick brass bands, mandating that brass #B08D57 must only be used for thin rules and small details; this was reaffirmed on 2025-06-19 with the approval of a 2px brass rule for the website hero banner. Margaret Hale approved a navy background for the 'Client alert social card' project on 2025-08-11. Furthermore, as of 2025-12-01, Margaret Hale prohibits the use of Christmas red and Christmas green in holiday designs to ensure inclusivity. As of 2025-12-05, David Whitford approved a navy card with a thin brass line for the 'Year-end digital holiday card' project. On 2026-07-13, Priya Raman approved a Litigation practice LinkedIn banner featuring a navy background and a thin brass rule. As of 2026-09-08, Margaret Hale prohibits the use of brass color for date lines on cream backgrounds due to poor readability, mandating navy text for date lines instead.

[Typography] Hale & Whitford LLP headlines must avoid bold sans-serif typefaces, preferring a professional and restrained aesthetic. As of 2025-06-06, David Whitford has mandated the removal of all sans-serif typography and lowercase text from designs, superseding the previous exception for website hero banners approved by Margaret Hale earlier that day. On 2025-06-11, Margaret Hale established a design rule for the website hero banner refresh project requiring a modern structure combined with traditional typography, which is reflected in the current use of Garamond in sentence case as approved by Priya Raman. This preference for Garamond in sentence case was reaffirmed by Priya Raman on 2026-07-13 for the Litigation practice LinkedIn banner.

[Typography] Hale & Whitford LLP uses Garamond as the primary typeface. As of 2026-03-05, Margaret Hale has mandated a heavier font weight for all text under 24px to ensure readability on mobile devices, as the standard serif font appears too thin. As of 2025-12-05, David Whitford approved the use of Garamond for the 'Year-end digital holiday card' project. On 2026-03-09, Priya Raman approved the use of Garamond Medium for body copy in the 'Recruiting post for summer associates' project.
[Typography] Hale & Whitford LLP uses italic Garamond for pull quotes in partner spotlight carousels, as approved by Margaret Hale on 2025-11-12.

[Imagery] Hale & Whitford LLP imagery should avoid stock photography of gavels, scales of justice, and handshakes, as the firm considers these symbols to be clichés. Additionally, the firm strictly prohibits the use of clip-art icons in design drafts, requiring professional imagery such as typography or real photography instead, as confirmed by David Whitford and Priya Raman on 2025-04-07. As of 2025-06-02, Margaret Hale has rejected oil-portrait style photography, requesting a more modern aesthetic that aligns with industry standards. Furthermore, as of 2025-11-03, David Whitford mandates that partner portraits must be formal, featuring subjects in suits against neutral backdrops, while strictly prohibiting candid or casual expressions. Finally, as of 2025-11-07, Priya Raman requires partner portrait photos to be black-and-white or desaturated to match the navy brand color, rejecting full-color photos as they appear like stock photography.

[Layout] Hale & Whitford LLP website hero banners should utilize an asymmetric layout with ample whitespace, as approved by Margaret Hale on 2025-06-06 and reaffirmed by Priya Raman on 2025-06-11. Additionally, the Litigation practice LinkedIn banner approved by Priya Raman on 2026-07-13 utilizes an asymmetric layout with the logo positioned at the bottom-right.

[Imagery] Hale & Whitford LLP mandates that holiday-themed designs must be inclusive of all clients, strictly prohibiting religious imagery, Christmas red, and Christmas green, as mandated by Margaret Hale on 2025-12-01.

[Copy] Hale & Whitford LLP brand tone is quiet and confident, targeting established families and business owners. Headlines must be restrained and professional, specifically avoiding exclamation marks to prevent a 'shouting' appearance (as requested by Margaret Hale on 2025-02-10). Additionally, David Whitford rejected drafts with excessive text (e.g., six paragraphs) on 2025-04-07, requiring brevity. As of 2025-08-07, Margaret Hale has mandated that all-caps and the word 'urgent' are prohibited, as the firm's tone must be informative rather than alarming. As of 2025-12-01, Margaret Hale mandates the use of the phrase 'Season's greetings' for holiday communications. As of 2025-12-05, David Whitford confirmed the tone for the 'Year-end digital holiday card' is 'Tasteful', featuring the text 'With gratitude for the year'. As of 2026-03-02, Priya Raman prohibits the use of emojis and the word 'squad' to maintain the firm's professional brand voice.
